what_this_is: Every number the chassis tool uses to make a decision, with where it came from. A layer of the theory stack counts as established only when all of its parameters are registered here. The registry exists because the project's own theory-stack document concluded that the equations are published and the parameters are the actual work; an unregistered number is a number nobody can check.

how_to_read_a_grade.A: Measured in S. cerevisiae, primary publication identified, uncertainty or spread stated.
how_to_read_a_grade.B: Measured in S. cerevisiae, or taken from a named public database, with the source identified but no uncertainty available.
how_to_read_a_grade.C: Measured in a different organism and transferred to yeast, or a published model constant whose applicability to yeast has not been checked. Every C is an assumption wearing a number's clothes.
how_to_read_a_grade.D: No external source. A value chosen inside this project because the code needed something. These are the dangerous ones, because the output looks identical to a grade-A output.

audit_rule: A parameter with grade D must not appear in any statement the tool presents as a prediction. It may appear in a heuristic that is labelled as a heuristic.

parameters.name: Heterologous protein mass fraction at which yeast growth stops
parameters.source_quote: These proteins can be expressed at levels exceeding 40% of total protein while maintaining yeast growth
parameters.citation_status: Quote recorded, publication not identified in this project. A number whose paper cannot be named cannot be checked by a reader.
parameters.notes: The quote says 'exceeding 40%', so 0.40 is a lower bound being used as a ceiling. That makes the derived optimum of 20% a lower bound too.

parameters.name: Heterologous protein mass fraction at which E. coli growth stops
parameters.organism_used_for: E. coli only; shown for comparison, not applied to the chassis
parameters.source_quote: we estimated the maximum capacities of the cell for heterologous expression to be 46% of the total RNA and the 33% of the total protein
parameters.citation_status: Quote recorded, publication not identified in this project.
parameters.notes: Not used for any chassis decision. Retained as the comparison that makes the growth-law shape visible.

parameters.name: Maximum fraction of cell protein achievable by one single protein
parameters.source_quote: The limits of some glycolytic proteins were up to 15% of the total cellular protein
parameters.citation_status: Quote recorded, publication not identified in this project.
parameters.notes: Measured for NATIVE glycolytic enzymes, which are highly optimised for expression in this host. Applying it as a ceiling for a heterologous protein is an extrapolation the source does not make.

parameters.name: Number of independent CRISPR guides that can be active before fold-repression degrades
parameters.source_quote: In E. coli, CRISPRi cannot support more than about a dozen simultaneous gRNAs before the fold repression of any individual gRNA drops below 10x
parameters.citation_status: Quote recorded, publication not identified in this project.
parameters.uncertainty: The source says 'about a dozen', which is a word, not a measurement with a spread.
parameters.notes: A bacterial dCas9 titration result applied to a yeast chassis. Theory-stack layer 3 (resource competition) is the layer that would derive this number for yeast instead of importing it.

parameters.name: Kyte-Doolittle hydropathy scale
parameters.organism_measured_in: not organism-specific; derived from water-vapour transfer free energies and interior-exterior residue distributions
parameters.primary_citation: Kyte J, Doolittle RF (1982) A simple method for displaying the hydropathic character of a protein. J Mol Biol 157:105-132
parameters.notes: The scale itself is published and standard. What this project does WITH it (the window sizes and thresholds below) is not.

parameters.name: Mean hydropathy above which a 9-residue N-terminal window is called a signal-peptide h-region
parameters.citation_status: No source. Chosen so that human preproinsulin scores positive and mature erythropoietin scores negative.
parameters.uncertainty: Unknown. Two proteins is not a calibration set.
parameters.notes: Validated indirectly: scripts/validate_features.py scored signal-peptide calls 21 of 24 against UniProt. That is a measured hit rate on a 24-protein panel, not a derivation of 1.6. The replacement is SignalP, which is a trained model with published performance.

parameters.name: Window length scanned for the signal-peptide h-region
parameters.citation_status: No source. Chosen because averaging over a longer fixed N-terminal slice diluted short h-regions and made preproinsulin score negative.
parameters.notes: Signal-peptide h-regions are described in the literature as roughly 7 to 15 residues, so 9 sits inside the published range. That is a consistency check, not a citation.

parameters.name: Window length scanned for a transmembrane helix
parameters.citation_status: No source recorded. 19-21 residues is the conventional length of a helix spanning a lipid bilayer, but this project did not cite it.
parameters.notes: Replacement is DeepTMHMM, which has published benchmark performance.

parameters.name: Mean hydropathy above which a 19-residue window is called transmembrane
parameters.citation_status: No source. Reuses the signal-peptide threshold for a different structural question, which is convenience rather than reasoning.
parameters.notes: A signal-peptide h-region and a transmembrane helix are different objects. Using one number for both is a shortcut this registry exists to expose.

parameters.name: How far from the N-terminus the signal-peptide scan runs
parameters.notes: Also sets where the transmembrane scan starts (offset 25) when a signal peptide was called, to avoid counting the signal peptide as a membrane helix.

parameters.name: Protein length above which the large-coding-sequence module is required
parameters.notes: This threshold decides whether an engineered module gets built. It is a round number with no measurement behind it, and it is the clearest example of why this registry was needed.

parameters.name: N-linked glycosylation sequon
parameters.citation_status: Consensus motif, widely published, specific citation not recorded here.
parameters.uncertainty: Occupancy is not predicted by the motif. A sequon may be unoccupied.
parameters.notes: Measured against UniProt in reports/02-feature-validation.md: 43 of 45 annotated sites recovered (96% recall), 72% precision. The precision shortfall is exactly the occupancy problem: the motif is present, the sugar is not.

parameters.name: Selective-constraint penalties for codon-anticodon wobble pairing
parameters.unit: dimensionless penalty, 0 = no penalty, 1 = no pairing
parameters.organism_measured_in: fitted across genomes by the method's authors
parameters.source_type: published model constants, taken from the authors' own implementation
parameters.primary_citation: dos Reis M, Savva R, Wernisch L (2004) Solving the riddle of codon usage preferences: a test for translational selection. Nucleic Acids Res 32:5036-5044. Values read from the authors' R implementation, github.com/mariodosreis/tai, R/tAI.R, retrieved 2026-11-03.
parameters.uncertainty: The authors describe these as optimised values. This project has not verified whether yeast was in the optimisation set.
parameters.notes: The 0.89 term applies only to the prokaryote isoleucine ATA special case and is NOT used for yeast (the authors' eukaryote code path, sking=0, skips it). Read from source code rather than retyped from the paper text, so the values are the ones the method actually runs with.

parameters.name: tRNA gene copy numbers per anticodon, S. cerevisiae
parameters.primary_citation: GtRNAdb (Genomic tRNA Database), genome Scere3 / sacCer3, https://gtrnadb.ucsc.edu/genomes/eukaryota/Scere3/, retrieved 2026-11-03. Underlying predictions by tRNAscan-SE.
parameters.uncertainty: These are tRNAscan-SE PREDICTIONS of tRNA genes, not measurements of tRNA molecules. Gene copy number is a proxy for tRNA abundance, and the two are correlated but not equal. Abundance also changes with growth rate and condition, which a fixed table cannot represent.
parameters.notes: Checksum: the file totals 270 elongator genes; adding the 5 initiator methionine genes excluded from elongation gives the 275 GtRNAdb reports independently in its Overview box. scripts/params.py asserts this on load.

parameters.name: Initiator methionine tRNA genes excluded from the elongation model
parameters.primary_citation: GtRNAdb Scere3 summary reports anticodon CAT as 5 initiator plus 5 elongator.
parameters.notes: A stated modelling decision rather than a raw database value: initiator tRNA does not participate in elongation, so it is removed. Recorded here so the departure from the raw page is visible.

what_this_registry_does_not_contain: Any parameter for theory-stack layers 1a (transcription thermodynamics), 1b (yeast translation initiation), 3 (resource competition), 4 (enzyme-constrained metabolism), 5 (secretory costs) or 6 (noise). Those layers are specified and unimplemented, so they have no parameters to register.

Any measured proteome cost for the five engineered modules. Every module in chassis/chassis-v1.json still carries cost_status 'not measured'. This is the single largest hole in the chassis and the reason the budget constraint cannot be checked against a real configuration.
Uncertainty ranges for most entries. Most sources state a single number, and this registry does not invent a spread for them.

Primary publication identifiers for the four numeric constants inherited from earlier protocol documents: the yeast and E. coli proteome ceilings, the single-protein ceiling, and the regulator count. The quotes were recorded; the papers were not. The audit counts five sourced parameters without an identified paper, the fifth being the glycosylation sequon motif, which is an established consensus rather than one measurement. Until this is fixed a reader cannot independently verify the project's load-bearing constants.
